subject.title: [Bug] v2026.5.22 启动后 Gateway CPU 持续 100%+，导致请求延迟飙升 50-100 倍

question: Should OpenClaw keep eager provider-auth startup warming by default, or accept the lazy hook-only/default-off startup behavior proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88514 to protect gateway responsiveness?
rationale: The narrow fix is technically clear, but it changes when prepared provider-auth state is populated for upgraded gateways, which is a compatibility-sensitive startup/auth-provider product contract.

options.title: Accept Hook-Only Default
options.body: Make normal gateway startup skip unsolicited provider-auth warm work while preserving explicit startup warm and auth-profile failure rewarm paths.

options.title: Keep Eager Startup Warm
options.body: Leave eager provider-auth startup warming as the default and continue relying on worker-thread/off-main-thread mitigations despite the reported startup CPU and latency regressions.

options.title: Require Explicit Upgrade Proof First
options.body: Hold the fix until maintainers get fresh-install and upgrade proof that lazy provider-auth discovery does not break expected auth/model availability.

recommendation.title: Accept Hook-Only Default
recommendation.body: Make normal gateway startup skip unsolicited provider-auth warm work while preserving explicit startup warm and auth-profile failure rewarm paths.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the active maintainer PR for this exact startup-auth default tradeoff and has current branch proof attached there.
